data.title: DSI serves summons on PP's Somchart
data.description: <p>The Department of Special Investigation (DSI) has successfully served a summons on People's Party (PP) MP for Phuket Somchart Techathavorncharoen, ordering him to give a statement next Monday in connection with an investigation into suspected nominee arrangements involving property companies in Phuket.</p>

data.title: Fire-damaged site sealed for debris clean-up
data.description: <p>Authorities have declared the area surrounding the fire-damaged Khlong Thom Centre building a restricted fire zone as they move in to dismantle debris.</p>

data.title: Bulbul breeding allowed, trapping banned
data.description: <p>The removal of Thailand's red-whiskered bulbul (nok krong hua juk) from the protected wildlife list does not allow people to trap the birds in the wild, Natural Resources and Environment Minister Suchart Chomklin stressed.</p>

data.title: DSI officers face investigation over exam fraud links
data.description: <p>Justice Minister Pol Lt Gen Rutthapon Naowarat has ordered an investigation into two Department of Special Investigation (DSI) officers allegedly linked to local-government exam fraud, while People's Party MP Rangsiman Rome examines possible wider political involvement.</p>

data.title: Migrant group urges law to protect fishing workers
data.description: <p>The Migrant Working Group (MWG) has submitted a proposed marine fishing labour protection bill to the People's Party (PP), seeking parliamentary action against exploitation and forced labour.</p>

data.title: Court revives NBTC chief's qualification case
data.description: <p>The Supreme Administrative Court has overturned a lower court's refusal to hear a challenge by the chairman of the National Broadcasting and Telecommunications Commission (NBTC) against the NBTC selection committee's ruling on his qualifications.</p>

data.title: Pheu Thai dismisses coalition fears
data.description: <p>Pheu Thai Party (PT) leader Julapun Amornvivat has dismissed concerns over government instability, saying a dinner planned for coalition leaders on Sunday is intended to improve communication and coordinate government work, not prepare for a no-confidence debate.</p>

data.title: Parties agree on initial House targets
data.description: <p>The opposition has named Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Digital Economy and Society Minister Chaichanok Chidchob as initial no-confidence targets over concerns about government accountability and policy implementation.</p>

data.title: Low-carbon shift 'a growth engine'
data.description: <p>The low-carbon transition should be treated as a new growth engine for Thailand rather than an environmental obligation, Joint Standing Committee on Commerce, Industry and Banking (JSCCIB) co-chairman Payong Srivanich said on Wednesday.</p>

data.title: Households to face insurance survey
data.description: <p>The Interior Ministry has ordered a nationwide survey of households without house numbers by Sept 15 to support a planned national disaster insurance system covering about 30 million households.</p>

data.title: Rupert Murdoch 'very happy' to be played by Guy Pearce in new film
data.description: VENICE - Australian-born media mogul Rupert Murdoch is "very happy" to see compatriot Guy Pearce play him in a new, largely sympathetic movie about his early business life, the actor said on Wednesday.

data.title: Thais, Singapore deepen ties
data.description: <p>Thailand and Singapore have agreed to deepen cooperation in four key areas covering energy, investment, defence and regional affairs.</p>

data.title: Trump floats renaming Strait of Hormuz as 'Trump Strait'
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - President Donald Trump on Wednesday suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz as "Trump Strait," asserting US control of the vital waterway even as fighting raged there with Iran.

data.title: Uber says laying off 'about 10%' of workforce worldwide
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Ride-hailing giant Uber will be laying off around 10 percent of its staff as part of "significant organizational changes," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in a message to employees released on Wednesday.

data.title: Nicaraguan ‘reform’ bars opposition from elections
data.description: ⁠Nicaragua’s Congress ⁠has passed a constitutional ​reform that bans opposition parties from participating in elections and extends ​the presidential term from six to ‌seven years, a move that had previously drawn criticism from the United States and other countries in the region.

data.title: Tiger Woods forfeits driver’s licence for 5 years
data.description: Tiger Woods ​has given up his driver’s licence for five years under a plea agreement reached in connection with a car accident earlier this year in Florida.

data.title: US run by ‘least qualified people’, says George Clooney
data.description: VENICE - Veteran film star George Clooney said on Wednesday the United States would surmount an “unfortunate” time in its history under the Trump administration, calling it a government run by the “least qualified people”.

data.title: Missing passengers ‘likely went down with sunken ferry’
data.description: ISTANBUL - The 20 people missing from a passenger ferry that capsized off northern Cyprus likely went down with the ship, officials said Wednesday as rescue operations continued for a fourth day.

data.title: US sailors warmly welcomed in Pattaya
data.description: More than 5,000 US Navy personnel from the USS Abraham Lincoln have begun making their way into Pattaya, where they are expected to pour about 100 million baht into the local economy during five days of long-overdue shore leave.

data.title: Cabinet changes location of Korat floral expo
data.description: The cabinet has agreed to change the venue for an international floral exhibition in Nakhon Ratchasima, a decision that has shocked and angered residents.

data.title: Bus crash in Egypt’s Sinai region kills 22
data.description: CAIRO - A passenger bus overturned on a desert highway in Egypt’s eastern Sinai Peninsula on Wednesday, killing 22 people and injuring 28 others, authorities said.

data.title: New York City to ban AI in schools through Grade 8
data.description: NEW YORK - New York City will ban the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for students in public schools through eighth grade, a source close to the matter told Agence France-Presse (AFP) on Wednesday, confirming US media reports.

data.title: 10 missing as Turkish cargo ship sinks after collision
data.description: ISTANBUL - A Turkish cargo ship sank in the Marmara Sea near Istanbul after colliding with a second vessel, with rescuers searching for its 10 crew members, Turkish officials said Wednesday.

data.title: Gary Glitter pleads not guilty to UK child sex offences
data.description: LONDON - ⁠Former ⁠British pop ​star Paul Gadd, better known ​by his ‌stage name Gary Glitter, pleaded not guilty in a London court on Wednesday to eight ​charges ⁠of historic sex offences against a young girl.

data.title: Ebola death toll passes 3,000 in DR Congo
data.description: KINSHASA - The deadliest ever Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has now claimed the lives of more than 3,000 people, according to the latest official figures released on Wednesday.

data.title: Accused agent for corporate ‘mule accounts’ arrested
data.description: A woman accused of acting as an agent for a major corporate mule-account network, backed by a Chinese financier, has been arrested in Bangkok. Police say accounts supplied by the network had been linked to more than 27 fraud cases.

data.title: Who Holds the Brakes? Building Trust in Thailand’s AI Economy
data.description: Sigve Brekke, Group CEO of True Corporation Plc. , shared his perspectives in a keynote titled “From Algorithmic Shock to Ethical Shift: Why Trust Is the Currency of Thailand’s Digital Future” at GCNT EXPO 2026, held under the theme “FROM SHOCK TO SHIFT – Sustainable Transition in a Fractured World”. The event was organized by the Global Compact Network Thailand (GCNT) at True Digital Park.

data.title: New York City to ban AI in public schools through eighth grade
data.description: NEW YORK — New York City will ban the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for students in public schools through eighth grade, a source close to the matter told Agence France-Presse ( AFP ) on Wednesday, confirming US media reports.

data.title: Wildfire haze forces 1.4 million Indonesian students into remote learning
data.description: JAKARTA - Around ⁠1.4 million ⁠students in six Indonesian provinces ​have shifted to online learning due to poor air quality triggered ​by forest and land fires, ‌an official said on Wednesday.
